title: (No AI) Instagram is adding an AI ‘assistant’ to tell you how to post
author: Mia Sato
content:
![An illustration of the Instagram logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/acastro_STK070__01.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Instagram is the latest social media platform to add built-in AI-powered features that will give users feedback on their posts. The company announced Wednesday that its standalone Edits app will now include an AI "creative assistant" that pulls in data from a user's Instagram account and offers suggestions on what to change.

Using the new assistant, creators can ask open-ended questions about what's trending on Instagram, why one video worked and another didn't, or what piece of content resonated most with their audience. The tool pulls in data and metrics such as likes, views, retention on videos, and shares. Instagram says it can spot pat …

title: (No AI) Here’s how tech leaders will self-police AI safety under Trump’s deal
author: Jess Weatherbed
content:
![Satya Nadella, chief executive officer of Microsoft Corp., from left, Greg Brockman, president and co-founder of OpenAI Inc., Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., US House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican from Louisiana, US President Donald Trump, Lisa Su, chair and chief executive officer of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), Nikesh Arora, chief executive officer at Palo Alto Networks Inc., and Elon Musk, chief executive officer of Tesla Inc., during a meeting with tech executives on artificial intelligence in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. The gathering follows a surge in concern about AI potentially posing a threat to humans. ](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/gettyimages-2297269621.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Anyone else getting “The Last Supper” vibes from this photo taken at the White House tech gathering? | Photographer: Tierney L. Cross/The Washington Post/Bloomberg via Getty Images

We now have the full details of the ["morally binding" AI safety deal](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/29/trump-ai-deal-tech-ceos-superintelligence) announced by President Trump yesterday, in which top executives agreed to self-regulate their artificial intelligence technology. The accord, officially titled the Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities, was [shared online](https://x.com/DavidSacks/status/2105060520327786914) by tech founder and presidential adviser David Sacks, and has been signed by Google's Sundar Pichai, Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI's Greg Brockman, XAI's Elon Musk, and Nvidia's Jensen Huang.
